656359.title: Long, Crawford
656359.description: Wikipedia: Long was born in Danielsville, Madison County, Georgia. He received his M.D. degree at the University of Pennsylvania in 1839. After observing the same physiological effects with diethyl ether ("ether") that Humphry Davy had described for nitrous oxide in 1800, Long used ether for the first time on March 30, 1842 to remove a tumor from the neck of a patient, James M. Venable, in Jefferson, Georgia. Long subsequently removed a second tumor from Venable and used ether as an anesthetic in amputations and childbirth. The results of these trials were published in 1848 in The Southern Medical and Surgical Journal. An original copy of this publication is held in the U.S. National Library of Medicine.

578516.description: The U.S. Census Monitoring Board, established by Congress in 1997, is a bipartisan board charged with monitoring Census 2000 operations and with reporting its findings to Congress. The Board is composed of eight Members: four appointed by the President, two appointed by the Speaker of the House of Representatives, and two appointed by the Majority Leader of the United States Senate. The Board began its work in 1998 and issued reports to Congress in February, April and October of 1999, March and April of 2000, and in April 2001. 578392.title: American Battle Monuments Commission
578392.description:
The American Battle Monuments Commission is a small independent agency of the Executive Branch of the federal government. It is responsible for:
  • commemorating the services of the American Armed Forces where they have served since April 6, 1917 (the date of U.S. entry into World War I)
  • through the establishment of suitable memorial shrines; designing, constructing, operating and maintaining permanent American military burial grounds in foreign countries;
  • for controlling the design and construction of U.S. military monuments and markers in foreign countries by other U.S. citizens and organizations, both public and private; and
  • encouraging the maintenance of such monuments and markers by their sponsors.
Source: ABMC.gov

578060.description: This category contains links to the candidates and campaigns for President of the United States in the year 2000 AD.   The President is the chief executive of the United States, with powers and duties enumerated under Article II of the United States Constitution. To be eligible for office, he or she must be a native-born citizen of the United States and a resident thereof for 14 years, and at least 35 years of age. The President and Vice-President are elected together.   When Americans vote for President and Vice-President, it should be noted, they do not actually vote for them but for a candidate's electors, who subsequently meet in state capitals after the general election and cast the official votes. Each state is allowed as many electors as it has Senators and Congressmen; thus, California has 54 (52 members of the US House and 2 US Senators) and Delaware has 3 (1 member of the US House and 2 US Senators).   A candidate who wins a state's vote, no matter by how small a margin, is entitled to all the electors from that state-- which impacts the manner in which Presidential campaigns are conducted.

578526.description: The National Imagery and Mapping Agency (NIMA) provides timely, relevant, and accurate imagery, imagery intelligence, and geospatial information in support of military, national-level, and civil users.

578525.title: National Reconnaissance Office
578525.description: The National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) is the single, national program to meet US government needs through spaceborne reconnaissance.

links.title: National Reconnaissance Office (NRO)
links.description: Provides IMINT (imagery intelligence) to the Department of Defense and its various offices and departments. History, mission, news, FOIA information and imagery archive.

links.title: Defense POW/Missing Personnel Office (DPMO)
links.description: Official US Government website for Prisoner of War/Missing in Action (POW/MIA).

links.title: Department of Defense Education Activity (DoDEA)
links.description: The public school systems (DoDDS and DDESS) administered by the Department of Defense.

578528.title: Joint Chiefs of Staff
578528.description: A major element of the United States Department of Defense. The Joint Chiefs of Staff consist of the Chairman, the Vice Chairman, the Chief of Staff of the Army, the Chief of Naval  Operations, the Chief of Staff of the Air Force, and the Commandant of the Marine Corps. The collective body of the JCS is headed by the Chairman, who sets the agenda and presides over JCS meetings. The Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff is the principal military adviser to the President, Secretary of Defense, and the National Security Council (NSC).

578531.title: Office of the Secretary of Defense

links.title: Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology and Logistics (AT&L)
links.description: Supervises the DoD's acquisition process, research and development; advanced technology; test and evaluation; production; logistics; military construction; procurement; economic security; and atomic energy.

links.title: Director of Operational Test and Evaluation (DOT&E)
links.description: Responsible for reviewing and analyzing the results of tests conducted for each major DoD acquisition program; and oversight to ensure those programs confirm operational effectiveness and suitability for combat use.

links.title: Office of the Special Assistant for the Gulf War Illnesses
links.description: Provides recently-declassified documents that may be relevant to illnesses affecting Gulf War Veterans.

links.title: Defense Microelectronics Activity (DMEA)
links.description: Provides a broad spectrum of microelectronics services to DoD. The DMEA is located in Sacramento California.

links.title: Department of Defense Inspector General (DoD-IG)
links.description: Responsible for conducting, supervising, monitoring and initiating audits and investigations relating to the programs and operations of the DoD.

links.title: Defense Language Institute English Language Center (DLIELC)
links.description: The operational manager for training international military/civilian personnel to speak and teach English. Located at Lackland, AFB, TX.

links.title: Office of the Executive Secretary
links.description: Part of the Immediate Office of the Secretary of Defense and is the head of an organization known as the Executive Secretariat. The Executive Secretary provides direct administrative support to the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense.

links.title: Assistant to the Secretary of Defense for Intelligence Oversight ATSD(IO)
links.description: Responsible for the independent oversight of all intelligence, counterintelligence, and intelligence-related activities in the Department of Defense.

links.title: Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness (P&R)
links.description: Maintain the defense workforce; the 1.5 million active duty military and 1.5 million guard and reserve personnel, and the 800,000 civilians that support the Nation's military operations.

links.title: Office of the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller)
links.description: Responsible for the financial management and policy, Defense budget submission and execution, financial statements and business practices of the Department of Defense.

578530.title: Unified Combatant Commands
578530.description: A Unified Combatant Command is composed of forces from two or more services, has a broad and continuing mission and is normally organized on a geographical basis. The number of unified combatant commands is not fixed by law or regulation and may vary from time to time.

links.title: United States Pacific Command (PACOM)
links.description: Promotes peace, deters aggression, responds to crises and, if necessary, will fight and win to advance security and stability throughout the Asia-Pacific region.

links.title: United States Southern Command (SOUTHCOM)
links.description: Responsible for all U.S. military activities in South America and Central America. Encompasses nineteen countries, represents about one-sixth of the world's land mass and covers about seven million square miles, stretching 6,000 miles from Mexico's southern border to Cape Horn.

links.title: United States African Command (AFRICOM)
links.description: Administrative headquarters responsible to the Secretary of Defense for U.S. military relations with 53 African countries, focusing on war prevention rather than war-fighting.

links.title: United States Central Command (CENTCOM)
links.description: Responsible for U.S. security interests in 20 nations, stretching through the Arabian Gulf region into Central Asia.

links.title: United States Northern Command (NORTHCOM)
links.description: Plans, organizes, and executes homeland defense and civil support missions.

links.title: United States Strategic Command (STRATCOM)
links.description: STRATCOM deters military attack on the United States and its allies, and should deterrence fail, employs forces to achieve national objectives.

578761.title: Department of Education
578761.description:
The U.S. Department of Education (ED) was established on May 4, 1980 by Congress in the Department of Education Organization Act (Public Law 96-88 of October 1979).
  • Strengthen the Federal commitment to assuring access to equal educational opportunity for every individual;
  • Supplement and complement the efforts of states, the local school systems and other instrumentalities of the states, the private sector, public and private nonprofit educational research institutions, community-based organizations, parents, and students to improve the quality of education;
  • Encourage the increased involvement of the public, parents, and students in Federal education programs;
  • Promote improvements in the quality and usefulness of education through Federally supported research, evaluation, and sharing of information;
  • Improve the coordination of Federal education programs;
  • Improve the management of Federal education activities; and
  • Increase the accountability of Federal education programs to the President, the Congress, and the public.

links.title: U.S. Department of Education (ED)
links.description: Provides information about the Department's offices, programs, information and assistance services, funding opportunities, education statistics, publications, and education initiatives of the President and Secretary of Education.

links.title: Office of Hearings and Appeals
links.description: Provides an independent forum for the fair, impartial, equitable, and timely resolution of disputes involving the U.S. Department of Education and recipients of Federal Education Funds.

links.title: Office of Educational Technology (OET)
links.description: Focused on providing leadership in information technology at schools. Features initiatives such as the National Educational Technology Plan, along with programs for distance learning and Internet safety. Budget and legislation, grants, resources, state offices, and organizational contacts are provided.

links.title: No Child Left Behind
links.description: Offers details into the No Child Left Behind Act and features FAQs, and information on accountability, testing, reading, choice and supplemental educational services, safe school programs, newsletters, statistics and graphs.

links.title: Office of Indian Education
links.description: Supports the efforts of local educational agencies, Indian tribes and organizations, postsecondary institutions, and other entities.

links.title: Discretionary Grant Application Packages
links.description: Includes a table for each currently open grant competition with more detailed information and download packages.

links.title: Troops to Teachers
links.description: A U.S. Department of Education and Department of Defense program that helps eligible military personnel begin new careers as teachers in public schools, where their skills, knowledge and experience are most needed.

578773.title: External Relations Offices
578773.description: The US Department of Education's External Relations group are the Office of Legislation and Congressional Affairs and the Office of Intergovernmental and Interagency Affairs.

links.title: Office of Non-Public Education
links.description: Represents the interests, activities and needs of the private elementary and secondary school community, and consults with the private school community on student and teacher initiatives at ED. Publications, programs, private school locator service are highlighted.

links.title: Office of Legislation and Congressional Affairs (OLCA)
links.description: Serves as the principal advisor to the Secretary on education and other legislative matters before the Congress and as the Department's liaison in responding to the needs of Congress.

578774.title: Operations Offices
578774.description: The US Department of Education's Operations group are the Office of Management, the Office of the Chief Information Officer, and the Office of the Chief Financial Officer.

links.title: Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO)
links.description: Develops technological strategies and solutions that enable the Department of Education (ED) to provide world-class service to schools, students and their families.

links.title: Office of the Chief Financial Officer (OCFO)
links.description: Supervises the activities of major components, and serves as the principal advisor to the ED Secretary on all matters related to discretionary grant-making, cooperative agreements, and procurement, as well as financial management, financial control, and accounting.

578762.title: Program Offices
578762.description:
The U.S. Department of Education (ED) presently has the following major Program Offices;
  • Office of English Language Acquisition (OELA) [formerly, Office of Bilingual Education and Minority Languages Affairs (OBEMLA)],
  • Office for Civil Rights (OCR),
  • Institute of Education Sciences (IES) [formerly, Office of Educational Research and Improvement (OERI)],
  • Office of Innovation and Improvement (OII),
  • Office of Elementary and Secondary Education (OESE),
  • Office of Postsecondary Education (OPE),
  • Office of Safe and Drug-Free Schools (OSDFS),
  • Office of Special Educational and Rehabilitation Services (OSERS),
  • Office of Vocational and Adult Education (OVAE), and
  • Federal Student Aid (FSA).
Additional program offices are found within the above mentioned offices.

subcategories.title: Office of Elementary and Secondary Education
Office of Safe and Drug-Free Schools
Office of Special Education and Rehabilitative Services
Office of Vocational and Adult Education

578763.title: Institute of Education Sciences
578763.description: The Institute of Education Sciences, formerly, Office of Educational Research and Improvement (OERI), was established by the Education Sciences Reform Act of 2002.

links.title: National Center for Education Statistics (NCES)
links.description: Primary federal entity for collecting and analyzing educational data in the United States and other nations. Survey and program areas, electronic catalog, tables and figures, and locator services are provided.

links.title: Institute of Education Sciences (IES)
links.description: Advances the field of education research and features funding opportunities, details on the Education Sciences Reform Act of 2002, press releases, reports, and statistics.

links.title: Educational Resources Information Center (ERIC)
links.description: A national information system to provide access to education literature and resources. Search the database that contains more than 1 million abstracts of education-related documents and journal articles.

links.title: National Center for Education Evaluation and Regional Assistance (NCEE)
links.description: Evaluates the impact of federal programs, synthesizes and disseminates information from evaluation and research, and provides technical assistance to improve student achievement. Study plans, FAQs, and publications are featured.

578766.title: Office for Civil Rights
578766.description: The Office for Civil Rights (OCR) ensures equal access to education and to promote educational excellence throughout the nation through vigorous enforcement of civil rights.

links.title: Office for Civil Rights (OCR)
links.description: Ensures equal access to education and promoting educational excellence throughout the nation through vigorous enforcement of civil rights.

578771.title: Office of Elementary and Secondary Education
578771.description: The Office of Elementary and Secondary Education (OESE) promotes academic excellence, enhances educational opportunities and equity for all of America's children and families, and to improves the quality of teaching and learning by providing leadership, technical assistance and  financial support.

links.title: Office of Elementary and Secondary Education (OESE)
links.description: Promotes academic excellence, enhances educational opportunities and equity for all of America's children and families, and improves the quality of teaching and learning by providing leadership, technical assistance and financial support.

578765.title: Office of English Language Acquisition
578765.description: The Office of English Language Acquisition, Language Enhancement, and Academic Achievement for Limited English Proficient Students (OELA) (formerly the Office of Bilingual Education and Minority Languages Affairs (OBEMLA)) provides national leadership in promoting high quality education for the nation's population of English language learners (ELLs).   Traditionally, this population has been known as limited English proficient students (LEPs). OELA's mission is to include various elements of school reform in programs designed to assist the language minority agenda. These include emphasis on high academic standards, an improvement of school accountability, an emphasis on professional development, the promotion of family literacy, the encouragement of early reading, and the establishment of partnerships between parents and the community.

links.title: Office of English Language Acquisition, Language Enhancement, and Academic Achievement for Limited English Proficient Students (OELA)
links.description: Administers Title III of No Child Left Behind Act (2001). Features include statistics, funding opportunities, news, and education FAQs for limited-English proficient children.

578764.title: Office of Federal Student Aid
578764.description: The Office of Federal Student Aid (FSA) provides more than $60 billion of financial aid a year to college students.   The FSA programs include Pell grants, Stafford loans, PLUS loans, and the "campus-based" programs: Federal Work Study, Perkins loans, and Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunity grants.

links.title: Applying for Federal Student Aid
links.description: Applying using the online Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA), using the Federal School Code Search to look up codes for the colleges being considered, and additional assistance for completing the FAFSA.

links.title: Federal Student Aid (FSA)
links.description: Provides information about organization and progress in reinventing financial assistance programs, which provide financial aid to college students.

links.title: eZ-Audit FSA
links.description: A web-based paperless method for submission of financial statements and compliance audits to FSA. Features common submission errors, answers to FAQs, and steps for creating a submission.

links.title: FSA Student Portal
links.description: Provides student resources and links for preparing, choosing, applying, funding, attending, and repaying for financial aid.

578770.title: Office of Innovation and Improvement
578770.description: The Office of Innovation and Improvement (OII) is th entrepreneurial arm of ED, and makes strategic investments in promising educational practices through grants to states, schools, and community organizations. OII also leads the movement for greater parental options and information in education. This Office houses two dozen discretionary grant programs, and coordinates the public school choice and supplemental educational services provisions of the No Child Left Behind Act. Source: OII website

links.title: Office of Non-Public Education
links.description: Represents the interests, activities and needs of the private elementary and secondary school community at the Department and to consult with the private school community on the participation of students and teachers in programs and initiatives of the Department.

578768.title: Office of Postsecondary Education
578768.description: The Office of Postsecondary Education (OPE) provides financial aid information from the federal government to help students attend colleges and universities.  It also contains grant information and links to higher education institutions.

links.title: Office of Postsecondary Education (OPE)
links.description: Provides financial aid information from the federal government to help students attend colleges and universities. It also contains grant information and links to higher education institutions.

links.title: Higher Education Programs
links.description: Administers and supports projects that broaden access to higher education. HEP projects are awarded to institutions of higher education and non-profit organizations and agencies.

links.title: Institutional Development and Undergraduate Education Service
links.description: Administers programs funded under Title III, Title V, and the Robert C. Byrd Honors Scholarship program. Provides support improvements in educational quality, management, and financial stability at qualifying postsecondary institutions.

578769.title: Office of Safe and Drug-Free Schools
578769.description:
The Office of Safe and Drug-Free Schools (OSDFS) administers, coordinates, and recommends policy for improving quality and excellence of programs and activities that are designed to:
  • Provide financial assistance for drug and violence prevention activities and activities that promote the health and well being of students in elementary and secondary schools, and institutions of higher education. Activities may be carried out by State and local educational agencies and by other public and private nonprofit organizations.
  • Participate in the formulation and development of ED program policy and legislative proposals and in overall Administration policies related to violence and drug prevention; drafting program regulations.
  • Participate in interagency committees, groups, and partnerships related to drug and violence prevention, coordinating with other Federal agencies on issues related to comprehensive school health, and advising the Secretary on the formulation of comprehensive school health education policy.
  • Participate with other Federal agencies in the development of a national research agenda for drug and violence prevention.
  • Administer the Department's programs relating to citizenship and civics education.
  • Provide national leadership on issues and programs in correctional education.
Source: http://ed.gov/offices/OSDFS/

578767.title: Office of Special Education and Rehabilitative Services
578767.description: The Office of Special Education and Rehabilitative Services (OSERS) supports programs that assist in educating children with special needs, provides for the rehabilitation of youth and adults with disabilities, and supports research to improve the lives of individuals with disabilities.

links.title: Office of Special Education Programs (OSEP)
links.description: Focuses on the free appropriate public education of children and youth with disabilities from birth through age 21. This site provides information on current legislation, news, and meetings affecting disabled youth.

links.title: Office of Special Education and Rehabilitative Services (OSERS)
links.description: Offers a wide array of supports to parents and individuals, school districts and states in three main areas: special education, vocational rehabilitation and research. Highlights include programs and projects, publications and products.

links.title: Rehabilitation Services Administration (RSA)
links.description: Oversees formula and discretionary grant programs that help individuals with physical or mental disabilities to obtain employment and live more independently. Features programs, publications, grants and funding.

578772.title: Office of Vocational and Adult Education
578772.description: The Office of Vocational and Adult Education (OVAE) supports a wide range of programs and activities that help young people and adults obtain the knowledge and skills they need for successful careers and productive lives.

links.title: Office of Vocational and Adult Education (OVAE)
links.description: Supports a wide range of programs and activities that help young people and adults obtain the knowledge and skills they need for successful careers and productive lives.

links.title: Community College Liaison Office
links.description: The principal policy advisor on community college issues. Sections dealing with rural, Federal/state, technology, international, workforce development, campus connection, and diversity.

links.title: Career and Technical Education
links.description: Features information about technical education grant information, National Centers for Career and Technical Education (NCCTE), Career and Technical Student Organizations (CTSOs), career clusters, and vocational education facts.

links.title: Office of Science and Technology Information (OSTI)
links.description: Disseminates scientific and technical information from department research and development, and environmental programs. Search key collections, review project summaries, or view informational videos. Based in Oak Ridge, Tennessee.

links.title: U.S. Department of Energy
links.description: DOE's home page is organized by topic, including Data and Prices, Efficiency, Environmental Quality, National Security, Science and Technology, and Sources and Production.

links.title: Office of Policy and International Affairs
links.description: Information on energy policy development and implementation, international science and technology, libraries, and agreements.

links.title: Energy Sciences Network (ESnet)
links.description: A high-speed network serving thousands of Department of Energy scientists and collaborators worldwide.

links.title: Office of Environmental Management (EM)
links.description: Responsible for U.S. DOE environmental restoration, waste management,  technology development, and facility transition and management.

links.title: Office of Management
links.description: Information related to Department of Energy administration, human resources, training,  procurement, and related topics.

links.title: Chief Information Officer
links.description: DOE organization whose responsibilities include information technology and cyber security.

links.title: Hanford Site
links.description: On the  Columbia River in southeastern Washington state, managed by the DOE  Richland Operations Office. Served as a plutonium production complex for national defense for more than 50 years beginning with the Manhattan    Project. Now the world's largest environmental cleanup project.

links.title: Savannah River Site (SRS)
links.description: DOE facility located near Aiken, South Carolina. Also the home of the Savannah River Technology Center, an applied research and development laboratory.

578589.title: DOE National Laboratories
578589.description: Sites administered by the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) national laboratories. DOE's definition of what is and isn't a national laboratory seems to fluctuate slightly over time, so the organizations listed in this category include those that either are currently, or have been recently, on DOE's list of national laboratories and technology centers (http://energy.gov/engine/content.do?BT_CODE=OF_NLTC).

subcategories.title: Idaho National Engineering and Environmental Laboratory
Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education

links.title: DOE Information Bridge
links.description: Department of Energy full-text technical reports in physics, chemistry, materials, biology, environmental cleanup, energy technologies and others.

links.title: DOE Pulse
links.description: A bi-weekly bulletin covering scientific research and development at the Department of Energy's national laboratories. Features include research highlights, updates on collaborations among laboratories, and profiles of individual researchers.

links.title: National Laboratories and Technology Centers
links.description: DOE's list of laboratories and technology centers.

links.title: USA.gov Science Research RSS Feeds
links.description: A collection of RSS feeds from U.S. government research laboratories

578598.title: Ames Laboratory
578598.description: Entries associated with the U.S. Department of Energy's Ames Laboratory.   Ames Laboratory works in materials research, high-performance computing, and environmental science and management to find solutions to energy-related problems through the exploration of physics, chemistry, engineering, applied mathematics and materials sciences. Located in Ames, Iowa.

links.title: Ames Laboratory (AMES)
links.description: Works in materials research, high-performance computing, and environmental science and management to find solutions to energy-related problems through the exploration of physics, chemistry, engineering, applied mathematics and materials sciences. Located in Ames, Iowa.

links.title: Nondestructive Evaluation
links.description: Includes a staff directory, seminars, meetings, and programs.

links.title: Materials Preparation Center
links.description: Recognized for its unique capabilities in the preparation, purification, and characterization of rare earth, alkaline-earth, and refractory metal materials.

links.title: Materials Preparation Center
links.description: Recognized for its unique capabilities in the preparation, purification, and characterization of rare earth, alkaline-earth, and refractory metal materials.

links.title: ANL Managing Contractor
links.description: University of Chicago

links.title: Argonne National Laboratory (ANL)
links.description: ANL conducts research in four broad categories: basic science, scientific facilities, energy resources, and environmental management, with programs ranging from studies of the atomic nucleus to global climate change research. Located at sites in Argonne, Illinois, and Idaho Falls, Idaho.

links.title: ANL Library
links.description: Home page of the ANL library

links.title: ANL Image Collection
links.description: Collection of photographic images

links.title: Argonne Tandem-Linear Accelerator System (ATLAS)
links.description: The world's first superconducting accelerator for projectiles heavier than the electron.

links.title: Atmospheric Radiation Measurement Climate Research Facility
links.description: The Atmospheric Radiation Measurement Program helps to resolve scientific uncertainties related to global climate change

links.title: Center for Nanoscale Materials
links.description: The center offers advanced facilities and expertise to support independent and collaborative research efforts in the field.

links.title: Advanced Photon Source
links.description: A national synchrotron radiation research facility located at Argonne National Laboratory near Chicago, Illinois.

links.title: Irradiated Materials Laboratory
links.description: The Irradiated Materials Laboratory is equipped for handling, testing, and analyzing irradiated materials.

links.title: Nondestructive Evaluation Laboratories
links.description: The laboratory conducts research and development related to instruments and nondestructive evaluation techniques for characterizing materials and determining system parameters for energy systems.

links.title: Advanced Photon Source
links.description: National synchrotron-radiation light source research facility. Includes application for beam time and organization information.

links.title: Biosciences Division
links.description: Conducts multidisciplinary research that further increases understanding of the fundamental mechanisms of life and enables advances in health protection, environmental restoration, energy production, industrial processing, and other applications. Includes research information, publications, staff, intratent and contact details.

links.title: High Energy Physics Division
links.description: Conducts research in areas of both theoretical and experimental particle physics. The laboratory also works on the ATLAS, CDF, MINOS, Soudan 2 and ZEUS experiments.

links.title: Physics Division
links.description: Research programs in studying the properties of nuclei and atoms including using a heavy-ion accelerator to study the structure of the nucleus and how the nucleus is affected by spinning or heating it. Includes information on sections, particle accelerators, news, conferences, employment, photos and contact details.

links.title: Environmental Science
links.description: Conducts applied environmental research, assessment, and technology development, primarily for federal agencies that have responsibilities for energy development and use, natural resource management, or national defense.

links.title: Mathematics and Computer Science Division
links.description: Focused on increasing scientific productivity by providing intellectual and technical leadership in the computing sciences, including computer science, applied computational mathematics, and computational science.

578670.title: Bettis Atomic Power Laboratory
578670.description: Entries associated with the U.S. Department of Energy's Bettis Atomic Power Laboratory (BAPL)

links.title: Bettis Laboratory
links.description: BAPL supports the development and use of advanced propulsion systems for U.S. Navy Vessels by performing basic research; testing new components; and providing technical expertise during construction, maintenance and refueling.

578602.title: Brookhaven National Laboratory
578602.description: Entries associated with the U.S. Department of Energy's Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL)

links.title: Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL)
links.description: Creates and operates facilities for use by university, industrial, and government personnel in basic and applied research in the physical, biomedical, and environmental sciences, and in selected energy technologies. Located in Long Island, New York.

links.title: BNL Office of Educational Programs
links.description: Precollege, undergraduate, and graduate programs and opportunities.

links.title: BNL Image Library
links.description: Collection of photographic images.

links.title: Visitor's Guide to Brookhaven
links.description: Information about working at Brookhaven National Laboratory and living on the Laboratory site and on Long Island.

links.title: BNL Phone Book
links.description: Contact information for people and organizations at the laboratory.

links.title: Careers at BNL
links.description: Information about jobs and recruitment.

links.title: BNL News
links.description: Recent developments at the laboratory.

links.title: BNL Managing Contractor
links.description: Brookhaven Science Associates.

links.title: National Nuclear Data Center (NNDC)
links.description: Provides information services in the fields of low and medium energy nuclear physics to users in the United States and Canada. In particular, the Center can  provide information on neutron, charged-particle, and photonuclear reactions, nuclear structure, and decay data.

links.title: Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC)
links.description: RHIC drives two intersecting beams of gold ions head-on, in a subatomic collision.

links.title: Collider-Accelerator Department
links.description: Responsible for the operation of a suite of accelerators used for experiments. Features links to the individual accelerators with diagrams, photographs, and tours.

links.title: Information Technology
links.description: Provides expertise in computing hardware and software support, as well as telecommunications services for the entire Laboratory.

links.title: Physics Department
links.description: Carries out research in experimental and theoretical high energy, nuclear and condensed matter physics. Programs, projects and people are showcased.

links.title: Superconducting Magnet Division
links.description: Develops superconducting magnets for use in both particle accelerators and experimental facilities. People, programs, projects and contacts are featured.

links.title: Chemistry Department
links.description: Focuses on PET studies of the human brain, heterogeneous and homogeneous catalysis, studies of gas phase dynamics of reactive species, solar photoconversion and other chemistries.

links.title: Collider-Accelerator Department
links.description: Responsible for the operation of a suite of accelerators used for experiments. Features links to the individual accelerators with diagrams, photographs, and tours.

links.title: Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory (FNAL or Fermilab)
links.description: Fermilab explores the fundamental nature of matter and energy by providing leadership and resources for qualified researchers to conduct basic research at the frontiers of high energy physics. Located in Batavia, Illinois.

links.title: FNAL Phone Book - People
links.description: Contact information for people at the laboratory

links.title: Working with the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory
links.description: Information about research partnerships and business relationships

links.title: FNAL History
links.description: Background of the laboratory.

links.title: FNAL Phone Book - Organization
links.description: Contact information for organizations within the laboratory

links.title: FNAL Managing Contractor
links.description: Universities Research Association, Inc.

links.title: Visiting the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory
links.description: Information for visitors and tourists

links.title: FNAL Overview
links.description: General description of laboratory activities

links.title: FNAL News
links.description: Recent developments at the laboratory

links.title: Fermilab Publications
links.description: Index of publications available.

links.title: Fermilab Information Resources Department
links.description: Searchable index of physics preprints available for download in PDF format.

links.title: FermiNews
links.description: A biweekly magazine.

links.title: Collider Detector
links.description: The Collider Detector at Fermilab (CDF) experimental collaboration is committed to studying high energy particle collisions at the world’s highest energy particle  accelerator. The goal is to discover the identity and  properties of the particles that make up the universe and to  understand the forces and interactions between those  particles.

links.title: DZero Experiment
links.description: The DØ Experiment consists of a worldwide collaboration of scientists conducting research on the fundamental nature of matter. The experiment is located at the world's premier high-energy accelerator, the Tevatron Collider, at the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory (Fermilab) in Batavia, Illinois, USA. The research is focused on precise studies of interactions of protons and antiprotons at the highest available energies. It involves an intense search for subatomic clues that reveal the character of the building blocks of the universe.

links.title: Booster Neutrino Experiment (BooNE)
links.description: The goal of this experiment is to test for neutrino mass by searching for neutrino oscillations. Neutrino mass is important because it may lead to physics beyond the Standard Model. Masses in the range accessible to MiniBooNE will expand understanding of how the universe has evolved.

links.title: Pierre Auger Observatory
links.description: The Pierre Auger Cosmic Ray Observatory studies the universe's highest energy particles, which shower down on Earth in the form of cosmic rays.

links.title: Cryogenic Dark Matter Search
links.description: The goal of CDMS is to detect dark matter, which has only been detected through large-scale gravitational interactions.

links.title: Sloan Digital Sky Survey
links.description: Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) will eventually provide detailed optical images covering more than a quarter of the sky, and a 3-dimensional map of about a million galaxies and quasars.

links.title: Large Hadron Collider Accelerator
links.description: Fermilab's role in the Large Hadron Collider program.

links.title: Dark Energy Survey
links.description: The Dark Energy Survey aims to make precision measurements of dark energy using four independent techniques.

links.title: International Linear Collider
links.description: Fermilab has a leadership role in working with the U.S. and international particle physics communities and the U.S. Department of Energy Office of Science to design and build the proposed International Linear Collider.

links.title: Theoretical Astrophysics
links.description: The Fermilab Theoretical Astrophysics Group performs research at the confluence of astrophysics, cosmology, and particle physics.

links.title: Theoretical Physics
links.description: Listings events, academic programs, physics resources, contact information, etc.

links.title: MINOS Experiment and NuMI Beam
links.description: The MINOS Experiment is a long-baseline neutrino experiment designed to observe the phenomena of neutrino oscillations, an effect which is related to neutrino mass.

links.title: Fermilab - Proton Driver Study Group
